review_mode: Scheduled cloud dual-review; independent Codex desk
limitations: Confidence values are subjective evidence confidence, not return probabilities. News remains unweighted in the trading score.

The Strait of Hormuz update continues the existing middle-east-oil-supply-shock thread. Full text was verified from the original Reuters report because the linked Business Recorder copy was not directly retrievable in this cloud browser.
The 11:26 PKT Business Recorder PSX selloff item was available through the committed raw summary during this run, so it is used as broad-market context only and not as company-rating evidence.

The KSE-100 recomposition and Pakistan fuel-price stories are carried forward from the current session because they remain valid current-session reviewed evidence; they were not reinterpreted as new stories.
Stories not reviewed are not Neutral ratings.

reviewed_stories.title: PSX recomposes KSE-100 Index, effective October 1
reviewed_stories.linkage: direct for IMAGE and THCCL; irrelevant to POWER
reviewed_stories.reason: Image Pakistan Limited and Thatta Cement Company Limited are explicitly being added to the KSE-100 from October 1, which can improve benchmark visibility and may create index-rebalancing demand. Nishat Chunian Power Limited is NCPL, not Power Cement Limited (POWER).

reviewed_stories.title: Petrol price rises Rs4.1, HSD jumps Rs6.4 from Sept 16
reviewed_stories.reason: The ex-depot petrol and HSD price increases are directly relevant to PSO's core products, but the article gives no PSO-specific margin, volume, inventory or working-capital impact. A higher selling price alone is not enough to infer higher profit.

reviewed_stories.title: Oil slips on US stock build, Middle East disruptions limit losses
reviewed_stories.linkage: sector link for Oil & Gas Exploration; negative broad-market import and inflation backdrop
reviewed_stories.reason: Brent was still about $108 despite a large US inventory build because Saudi Yanbu loadings and the East-West pipeline disruption remained unresolved. The physical supply problem continues to support upstream oil-linked exposure while worsening Pakistan's imported-energy backdrop.

reviewed_stories.title: Strait of Hormuz ship crossings remain in single digits, data shows
reviewed_stories.linkage: sector link for Oil & Gas Exploration; negative broad-market import and inflation backdrop
reviewed_stories.reason: Visible Hormuz transits fell to four on Tuesday from seven a day earlier and a 10-day average of 18, with no VLCC or LNG tanker among the counted crossings. That is a material continuation of the supply-disruption thread and supports elevated crude risk, while increasing Pakistan's imported-energy exposure.

reviewed_stories.title: PSX: Selling continues as KSE-100 sheds over 800 points
reviewed_stories.linkage: broad-market context only; no company-specific rating
reviewed_stories.reason: The committed raw summary reported the KSE-100 down 857.46 points at 11:20 PKT, with selling across autos, cement, banks, exploration companies and OMCs amid escalating Middle East tensions. This is market reaction evidence, not a new company cash-flow event.

IMAGE.reason: Direct company link: Image Pakistan Limited will enter the KSE-100 effective October 1. Benchmark inclusion can improve visibility and may create rebalancing or index-tracker demand around the effective date, though the size of any flow is not guaranteed.

THCCL.reason: Direct company link: Thatta Cement Company Limited will enter the KSE-100 effective October 1. Benchmark inclusion can improve visibility and may create rebalancing or index-tracker demand around the effective date, while the actual flow magnitude remains uncertain.

OGDC.reason: Sector continuation: Brent remained near $108 and visible Hormuz transits fell to four, far below the recent average, while Saudi export-route disruption remained unresolved. That supports OGDC's upstream oil-linked exposure, though receivables and production mix remain separate risks.

PPL.reason: Sector continuation: Brent remained near $108 and visible Hormuz transits fell to four, far below the recent average, while Saudi export-route disruption remained unresolved. That supports PPL's upstream oil-linked exposure; this is a sector read, not a new company-specific earnings estimate.

MARI.reason: Sector continuation: crude remains near $108 and Hormuz traffic is severely constrained, supporting the upstream energy backdrop. Mari's gas-heavy production mix makes the direct crude sensitivity weaker than for more oil-linked producers, so confidence remains lower.

PSO.reason: Direct operating link: ex-depot petrol rose Rs4.10 per litre and HSD rose Rs6.41 effective September 16. The article does not disclose PSO-specific margin, volume, inventory or working-capital effects, so the price increase is operationally relevant but not enough for a defensible positive or negative earnings call.
